There was a great study made by Hunter on intelligence and whole life outcomes, including real income. There is a strong correlation, up to a point, but it's not deterministic.
Tl;dr - people with IQ of 110 will generally earn more than people with IQ 90, but it doesn't mean you're "supposed to be rich" after a certain point. It's just averages, and both poor and rich people exist across the entire IQ distribution, but with very different proportions.

Also there was a very interesting study on IQ outliers (IQ 140+) that tracked them for entire life since childhood. The hypothesis was that these "gifted" children will become over achievers, win Nobel prizes, solve complex problems, become millionaires running companies etc. The actual findings were very surprising - for vast majority of the people tracked (~80% of them) they didn't really achieve anything out of the ordinary, or the achievement levels were similar to average in general population. The 20% that did overachieve had one factor in common - rich parents.
High IQ alone doesn't equal outstanding life outcomes. High IQ + money equals outstanding results.
I don't remember the name of the lead researcher but it's a famous study, it ran for ~80 years IIRC.
